Retrieval augmented generation (RAG) pairs an LLM with new data sources to retrieve the most relevant document for a query. Generally, continual pretraining and RAG are orthogonal approaches to generate up to date responses. RAG methods increase the cost at inference time without changing the model while continual pretraining is the opposite. FreshLLMs (Vu et al., 2024) proposes a QA benchmark and argues that fast-changing knowledge requires a retrieval-based solution compared with slow-changing knowledge

biblStruct.note: 2022b) Another is to store edits in an explicit memory and learn to reason over them Continual pretraining can be crucial in reducing the cost of RAG by utilizing retrieval only on knowledge that changes faster than the rate of continual pretraining
